info.title: Helix app API
info.description: The same-origin `/_api/*` gateway a hosted app calls from the browser: identity, LLM, app data, connected accounts, the fetch proxy, and background jobs. Requests are made from the app's own origin and carry the `__Host-session` cookie.

servers.description: The app's own origin. The gateway is same-origin, so an app calls `/_api/*` relative to its page.

get.description:
How a static app learns who is signed in: the principal id, display name and email address, and nothing else. Use `id` to key data; never display it.

Requires the app's session.

302.description: A top-level navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, or an `Accept` that includes `text/html`) without a usable session is redirected into sign-in instead of receiving the 401.

401.description: No session, or the session no longer grants access to this app (`unauthorized`), or the session is due for a refresh (`refresh_required`). Reload the page so the browser navigates through sign-in.

404.description:
Not found. The request was not made on an app host, the app does not exist or has no live version, or this capability is not configured on this deployment. The reasons are deliberately indistinguishable.

- `text/plain`: `Not found`

410.description: The app is archived. The response carries `Clear-Site-Data` so the browser drops the app's cached UI and storage.

503.description: The edge has not loaded the app registry yet. Retry shortly.

post.description:
The platform's provider-neutral LLM call. `model` must be on the app's manifest allowlist; the edge routes it to the vendor that serves it and meters the call against the app's budget. The request must carry the app's own `Origin` (CSRF check).

Public apps accept anonymous callers; every other visibility mode requires the app's session.

200.description:
The completion: a JSON body when `stream` is false, otherwise an event stream.

- `application/json`: The whole completion (`stream: false`).
- `text/event-stream`: Sent when `stream` is true (the default). Named events, each `data:` line one JSON object:

- `event: delta` — `{ text }` (`LlmStreamDelta`), zero or more.
- `event: done` — `{ stopReason, usage }` (`LlmStreamDone`), terminal on success.
- `event: error` — `{ code, message }` (`LlmStreamError`), terminal on a failure after the stream started.

A failure before the first delta is answered with an error status instead of a stream.

The deployment's operator policy does not allow apps with this app's visibility mode.

429.description: The app's daily spend budget is exhausted (`quota_exceeded`), its rolling-hour burst budget is exhausted (`rate_limited`), the anonymous per-IP budget is exhausted on a public app (`rate_limited`), or the upstream model throttled the call (`rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`).

The edge has not loaded the app registry yet. Retry shortly.

post.description:
An OpenAI-compatible subset over the same policy, budget and metering as `/_api/llm/chat`. Point an OpenAI client's `baseURL` at `<app origin>/_api/openai/v1`; the session cookie authenticates, and the SDK's `apiKey` is ignored. Errors raised by this surface use OpenAI's error envelope; the session gate's 401 and the edge's 500 keep the platform's `ApiError` envelope.

Text chat only: tools, multimodal content, `json_object`, and the sampling parameters the platform cannot honor (`n`, `seed`, `logit_bias`, the penalties, `logprobs`) are refused with a 400 rather than dropped. The request must carry the app's own `Origin` (CSRF check).

Public apps accept anonymous callers; every other visibility mode requires the app's session.

externalDocs.description: OpenAI's API reference, which this surface follows for the fields it accepts.

200.description:
The completion: a JSON body unless `stream` is true.

- `application/json`: A `chat.completion` object.
- `text/event-stream`: Sent when `stream` is true. Each event is a `data:` line holding one `chat.completion.chunk` (`OpenAiChatCompletionChunk`): the first carries `delta.role`, then one per text delta, then one with `finish_reason`. When `stream_options.include_usage` is true a final chunk with empty `choices` carries `usage`. The stream ends with `data: [DONE]`. A failure after the stream started is sent as one `data:` line holding the OpenAI error envelope, with no `[DONE]`.

post.summary: Append an item to a collection
post.description:
Collections are write-only: an app can append items, and only the app's owner can read them, in the portal. There is no read, list or delete route, and the response carries no item id. Anonymous visitors of public apps may append. The request must carry the app's own `Origin` (CSRF check).

Public apps accept anonymous callers; every other visibility mode requires the app's session.

get.summary: List shared keys under a prefix
get.description:
Shared scope: app-wide keys every visitor the app admits can reach, limited to the keys and prefixes the app's manifest grants.

The prefix must be covered by one of the app's shared-read prefix grants; a literal key grant does not allow listing. Returns at most 200 keys per page, with versions and write times but no values.

Public apps accept anonymous callers; every other visibility mode requires the app's session.

get.summary: Open the consent flow for a provider
get.description:
The entry to the consent popup: a same-origin browser navigation, not a `fetch`. Open it in a popup (the `window.helix.connect` helper does). With a usable session and a provider the app binds, the popup is redirected to the provider's authorize URL; every other outcome renders a terminal page that posts its outcome to the opener.

The navigation must be same-origin: `Sec-Fetch-Site`, when sent, must be `same-origin`, and `Origin` or `Referer` must name the app's own origin. A shared-password session cannot connect accounts and is treated as signed out.

Requires the app's session.

parameters.name: ref

schema.description: The provider reference the app's manifest binds. A malformed reference answers the plain-text 404.

parameters.description: The provider reference the app's manifest binds. A malformed reference answers the plain-text 404.

parameters.name: attempt

schema.description: A correlation tag the outcome message echoes back. At most one.

parameters.description: A correlation tag the outcome message echoes back. At most one.

200.description: The caller is already connected, or the connection is not available to this app. A terminal page in the platform's chrome. It posts the outcome to the opener (`window.opener.postMessage`, a `ConnectOutcomeMessage`) and offers Close.

400.description: The `attempt` tag is malformed or repeated.

The consent attempt could not start (the platform's connection service failed or is not configured). A terminal page in the platform's chrome. It posts the outcome to the opener (`window.opener.postMessage`, a `ConnectOutcomeMessage`) and offers Close.

post.description:
The connect helper calls this when the consent popup closed without posting an outcome, so a late completion of that attempt cannot succeed. Only attempts this caller started can be cancelled. The request must carry the app's own `Origin` (CSRF check).

Requires the app's session.

get.summary: Read the caller's connection status for a provider
get.description:
Whether the signed-in user's next call to this provider will be sent with their connection, from the platform's own records; no call is made to the provider. `connected`: it will. `not_connected`: it would be refused with `connection_required`, so offer Connect. `not_available`: the app does not bind this provider, or the provider is not available. A shared-password session is treated as signed out.

Requires the app's session.

get.summary: Proxy a GET request to an external origin
get.description:
Calls an external origin the app's manifest grants, through the platform. Put the whole target URL after the prefix, either raw or percent-encoded: `fetch('/_api/fetch/https://api.example.com/v1/items?q=1')`. The call is same-origin, so it needs no CSP change. When the grant has a connection secret or a delegated user connection, the platform adds the credential; the app never sees it.

The method, the body and these request headers are forwarded: `accept`, `accept-language`, `anthropic-version`, `content-type`, `if-modified-since`, `if-none-match`, `user-agent`. Every other header, `Cookie` and `Authorization` included, is dropped. The edge also reads `Origin` (it must be the app's own, a CSRF check), the session cookie, and `Content-Length` (a declared body over the size cap is refused before the call).

The upstream's response comes back with its own status, headers and body, streamed. The platform removes `Set-Cookie`, `Location`, credential and hop-by-hop headers, and caching headers, and answers `Cache-Control: no-store`. Upstream redirects are not followed. A body over the size cap is truncated, because the status is already sent.

When the platform refuses a call instead, the body is a `FetchProxyError` JSON object: `{ code, message }`, with `provider` on the delegated-connection codes. The statuses below list the refusals; the platform's connection service can also answer `connection_required` (403), `replay` (409), `provider_misconfigured` (502) and `provider_unavailable` (503) with the same shape.

Public apps accept anonymous callers; every other visibility mode requires the app's session.

302.description: A top-level navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, or an `Accept` that includes `text/html`) without a usable session is redirected into sign-in instead of receiving the 401.

400.description:
The target URL is missing, malformed, or not http(s) (`bad_target`). Or the upstream's own response with this status, passed through.

- `application/json`: A `FetchProxyError` refusal, or the upstream's JSON body.
- `*/*`: The upstream's body, in its own media type.

401.description: No session, or the session no longer grants access to this app (`unauthorized`), or the session is due for a refresh (`refresh_required`). Reload the page so the browser navigates through sign-in.

403.description:
The target origin is not granted to the app, or the `Origin` is not the app's own (`forbidden`); or the grant needs a delegated connection the caller does not have (`connection_required`, with `provider`). Or the upstream's own response with this status, passed through.

The deployment's operator policy does not allow apps with this app's visibility mode.

- `text/plain`: `Forbidden`
- `application/json`: A `FetchProxyError` refusal, or the upstream's JSON body.
- `*/*`: The upstream's body, in its own media type.

404.description:
Not found. The request was not made on an app host, the app does not exist or has no live version, or this capability is not configured on this deployment. The reasons are deliberately indistinguishable.

- `text/plain`: `Not found`

410.description: The app is archived. The response carries `Clear-Site-Data` so the browser drops the app's cached UI and storage.

413.description:
The request body exceeds the size cap (`too_large`). Or the upstream's own response with this status, passed through.

- `application/json`: A `FetchProxyError` refusal, or the upstream's JSON body.
- `*/*`: The upstream's body, in its own media type.

429.description:
The app's daily fetch budget, or the anonymous per-IP budget, is exhausted (`rate_limited`). Or the upstream's own response with this status, passed through.

- `application/json`: A `FetchProxyError` refusal, or the upstream's JSON body.
- `*/*`: The upstream's body, in its own media type.

502.description:
The platform's egress or the upstream call failed (`upstream_error`). Or the upstream's own response with this status, passed through.

- `application/json`: A `FetchProxyError` refusal, or the upstream's JSON body.
- `*/*`: The upstream's body, in its own media type.

503.description:
The fetch capability is not configured on this deployment (`upstream_error`). Or the upstream's own response with this status, passed through.

The edge has not loaded the app registry yet. Retry shortly.

- `application/json`: A `FetchProxyError` refusal, or the upstream's JSON body.
- `*/*`: The upstream's body, in its own media type.

default.description:
The upstream's response, passed through with its own status, headers and body (streamed).

- `*/*`: The upstream's body.

post.description:
Background jobs run platform-owned job types for the app, asynchronously. Only a signed-in user may submit or read jobs; anonymous visitors and shared-password sessions are refused with 403 `forbidden`, and a job is visible only to the user who submitted it.

The body is the job's input, forwarded byte for byte. Send an `Idempotency-Key` to make a retry safe: a repeat with the same key and input returns the original job. Submissions are charged against the app's submission budget whatever their outcome. The request must carry the app's own `Origin` (CSRF check).

Refusals the jobs service makes are forwarded with their own status and a `JobRequestError` body; the statuses below list the ones a caller should expect.

Requires the app's session.

schema.description: The job server, `jobs` on this platform.

parameters.name: type

schema.description: The job type within the server, e.g. `fetch`. The app's manifest must grant it.

parameters.description: The job type within the server, e.g. `fetch`. The app's manifest must grant it.

parameters.name: idempotency-key

schema.description: An optional retry key, at most 128 bytes, not empty or whitespace.

requestBody.description: The job input as JSON, at most 65536 bytes. Its shape depends on the type; the schema below is the `jobs:fetch` input.

202.description: The job was accepted, or this is a keyed replay of an accepted job. Poll the snapshot.

302.description: A top-level navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, or an `Accept` that includes `text/html`) without a usable session is redirected into sign-in instead of receiving the 401.

400.description: No job server has this name (`job_server_unknown`), the `Idempotency-Key` is invalid (`idempotency_key_invalid`), or the input is not valid for the type (`payload_invalid`).

401.description:
The jobs service refused the platform's own signed request (a `JobRequestError` with `unauthorized`), which is a platform fault, not the caller's.

No session, or the session no longer grants access to this app (`unauthorized`), or the session is due for a refresh (`refresh_required`). Reload the page so the browser navigates through sign-in.

403.description:
The caller may not use jobs, the `Origin` is not the app's own, or the app's manifest does not grant this type (`forbidden`).

The deployment's operator policy does not allow apps with this app's visibility mode.

- `text/plain`: `Forbidden`

404.description:
Not found. The request was not made on an app host, the app does not exist or has no live version, or this capability is not configured on this deployment. The reasons are deliberately indistinguishable.

- `text/plain`: `Not found`

409.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was already used with different input (`idempotency_conflict`, with the existing job's `status` and `error`).

410.description: The app is archived. The response carries `Clear-Site-Data` so the browser drops the app's cached UI and storage.

413.description: The input exceeds the size limit (`payload_too_large`).

429.description: The app's submission budget is exhausted (`rate_limited`), or the jobs service has no capacity (`jobs_capacity_exceeded`).

503.description:
Background jobs are not enabled on this deployment (`jobs_disabled`), or the jobs service did not answer usefully (`jobs_unavailable`). Retry `jobs_unavailable`; a submission's outcome is then unknown.

The edge has not loaded the app registry yet. Retry shortly.
